records.primary_i_can: I can decide whether the forces are balanced or unbalanced.
records.i_can: I can decide whether the forces are balanced or unbalanced.
records.evidence_job: Determine whether the forces on the modeled object are balanced or unbalanced and connect that judgment to zero or nonzero net force.
records.student_action: Determine whether the forces on the modeled object are balanced or unbalanced and connect that judgment to zero or nonzero net force.
records.student_text: The cart is described as moving at constant speed, but inspect the supplied force arrows. Are the forces balanced or unbalanced? Cite the mismatch.
records.student_html:
The cart is described as moving at constant speed, but inspect the supplied force arrows. Are the forces balanced or unbalanced? Cite the mismatch.

  1. Unbalanced: the unequal opposing horizontal arrows imply a nonzero net force, which conflicts with constant-speed straight-line motion.
  2. Balanced because any object with two or more forces is automatically in equilibrium.
  3. Unbalanced because motion always requires a forward net force.
  4. No conclusion is possible from a force diagram.

choices.text: Unbalanced: the unequal opposing horizontal arrows imply a nonzero net force, which conflicts with constant-speed straight-line motion.
Balanced because any object with two or more forces is automatically in equilibrium.
Unbalanced because motion always requires a forward net force.
No conclusion is possible from a force diagram.

records.student_action: Explain how nonzero net force changes motion, diagnose an incorrect force explanation, and revise the explanation using accurate physics vocabulary and model reasoning.
records.student_text: A student says, “The cart is moving right, so the net force must point right.” Critique and revise the explanation using physics vocabulary.
records.student_html: A student says, “The cart is moving right, so the net force must point right.” Critique and revise the explanation using physics vocabulary.
records.answer: Motion direction and net-force direction are not the same thing. Net force determines the direction of acceleration/change in velocity; a cart can move right while a leftward net force slows it.

records.student_text: A rolling cart moves right while the net force points left. Predict how its motion changes while that net force acts. Justify using net force.
records.student_html: A rolling cart moves right while the net force points left. Predict how its motion changes while that net force acts. Justify using net force.
records.answer: Its velocity changes toward the left: if it is initially moving right, it slows; with enough time it can stop and then speed up left. The net force determines the direction of acceleration.
